description:
In his latest documentary "Iran and the Bomb," CNN’s Fareed Zakaria examines the state of Iran’s nuclear program amid the country’s war with the United States.

In June 2025, the US attacked three nuclear facilities in Iran. The full extent of the damage remains unknown, but Fareed points out that Iran retains the knowledge needed to rebuild its nuclear program. Plus, Fareed lays out what a future nuclear deal between Iran and the United States could look like – one modeled on President Obama’s landmark deal from 2015, from which President Trump later withdrew.

description:
W. Kamau Bell goes behind the walls of San Quentin, one of America's most notorious prisons, to meet the men inside. Hear from people who have spent most of their lives behind bars and see who they've become.

In W. Kamau Bell's own words: "I had a great time in prison. That’s something I never thought I’d say... Admittedly, I had a great time in prison at San Quentin because every night I was allowed to leave and go home. I didn’t have to live in the cramped cells. I didn’t have to figure out ways to navigate the horrible – and I mean horrible – food. I was able to focus instead on the men who I met there. They were all funny, smart, remorseful, resourceful, skilled and self-reflective in ways that most people that I meet on the outside are not."

Originally broadcast in April 2016.

description:
Kim Aris, the younger son of imprisoned democracy icon Aung San Suu Kyi, says he still doesn’t know where his mother is being held. For nearly six years, the ruling junta did not permit him to speak with her, until October, when they allowed for one 20-minute phone call. He's received no update on her status since, despite his regular demands to establish a formal line of communication.

Aris continues to call for greater international support for his mother's release and Myanmar’s fight for democracy following the 2021 military coup. CNN’s Heather Law reports.

description:
Vice President JD Vance has given serious consideration to not running for president in 2028 after last week’s calamitous midterm elections, people close to him tell CNN. 

While Vance has yet to make up his mind, interviews with roughly a dozen allies and advisers reveal a vice president wrestling with his political ambitions, the fracturing of the MAGA coalition and the demands of fatherhood. They described him as deeply committed to rebuilding the movement that won in 2024 but uncertain over whether he should be the one to lead it. 

CNN's Alayna Treene reports and CNN's Dana Bash and Wolf Blitzer lead panel discussions on Vance's future.
